raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder (32-layer ViT + aligner) runs replicated on every TP rank and is host-bound:
hundreds of small launches per image, a host-to-device copy of the rotary tables and `cu_seqlens` per call, and
four boolean-mask writes that each sync the host while the image span is assembled. Host jitter on one rank then
becomes collective wait on the other ranks in the first LM layer after the encoder. In a TP4 trace of a
768x1024 image, rank 0 spent about 30 ms in that all-reduce, longer than the encoder itself.

## Modifications

- `DeepseekV41ViTCudaGraphRunner` (new, `multimodal/deepseek_v41_vit_cuda_graph_runner.py`) replays vision
  tower + aligner + span assembly as one graph per `(n_vit_h, n_vit_w)` grid.
  - On by default on CUDA and ROCm; off with `--disable-cuda-graph`. No new server args or env vars.
  - A grid is captured on its second sighting, so one-off sizes stay eager and pay no capture cost.
  - At most 16 grids are kept (LRU); graphs share one private memory pool.
  - A capture that fails is logged once and that grid stays eager.
  - Capture uses `capture_error_mode="thread_local"`, since other threads keep issuing CUDA calls.
  - The returned span is cloned, because spans live on in the multimodal embedding cache.
- `assemble_image_span` builds `[start] + ([features] * w + [newline]) * h + [end]` with two `cat`s instead of
  four boolean-mask writes. It produces the same layout as `image_token_types` (bit-exact, unit-tested) with no
  host sync. The eager path uses it as well.
- Rotary tables and attention metadata are cached on device per grid (`get_vision_inputs`), so neither path
  copies them per call, and the graph never records a host-to-device copy.

## Accuracy Tests

The graph replays the same kernels as the eager path, so outputs are bit-exact with eager on the tested grids.

| MMMU (TP4, MI350X) | Score |
|---|---|
| main | 0.7539 |
| this change | 0.7678 (n=1) |

The difference is within run-to-run noise of the end-to-end eval (batch composition varies between runs).

TODO before ready: re-run MMMU with this branch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, MI350X, `bench_serve` with `sglang-oai-chat`, one random image per request, sizes
512x512 / 768x1024 / 2048x1600. Measured with a prototype of this change that has the same graph scope (tower +
aligner + span, per-grid capture). Relative to main:

| | Change vs main |
|---|---|
| Median TTFT, 5 rows (c4–c64) | 16–31% lower |
| Rank-0 all-reduce after the encoder (768x1024) | 30.5 ms → 2.9 ms |
| Encoder time alone, one GPU (1521 / 4070 / 8343 patches) | −16% / −3% / −3% |
| Capture time per grid | ≤ 230 ms |
| Graph pool per grid | ≤ 0.6 GiB |

Most of the end-to-end gain comes from removing rank-to-rank skew rather than from the encoder getting faster
on one GPU.

TODO before ready:
- Re-measure with this branch (full sweep, main vs PR).
- Validate on an NVIDIA GPU. Capture has not run on CUDA yet; a failed capture falls back to eager.

Not in this PR (follow-ups): compiled pointwise ops in the encoder (not bit-exact), and data-parallel or batched
encoding for steps with several images.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
  `test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v41_vit_graph.py` (CPU): span layout vs `image_token_types`,
  capture on second sighting, no aliasing between returned spans, eager fallback after a failed capture, LRU eviction.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+"""Per-grid CUDA graph runner for the DeepSeek-V4.1 image encoder."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from collections import OrderedDict
+from typing import Any, Callable, Tuple
+
+import torch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# (patches, n_vit_h, n_vit_w) -> LLM span of the image.
+EncodeFn = Callable[[torch.Tensor, int, int], torch.Tensor]
+# (n_vit_h, n_vit_w, device) -> device tensors the encoder reads for that grid.
+InputsFn = Callable[[int, int, torch.device], Any]
+
+
+class DeepseekV41ViTCudaGraphRunner:
+    """Replays vision tower + aligner + span assembly as one graph per grid.
+
+    The encoder is replicated on every TP rank and host-bound (hundreds of
+    small launches per image), so host jitter on one rank becomes collective
+    wait on the others. A grid is captured on its second sighting, so one-off
+    sizes stay eager; a failed capture stays eager for that grid.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        encode: EncodeFn,
+        inputs: InputsFn,
+        *,
+        capacity: int = 16,
+        min_hits: int = 2,
+    ) -> None:
+        if capacity <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"capacity must be positive, got {capacity}")
+        if min_hits <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"min_hits must be positive, got {min_hits}")
+        self.encode = encode
+        self.inputs = inputs
+        self.capacity = capacity
+        self.min_hits = min_hits
+        # (n_h, n_w) -> (graph, static_patches, static_span, inputs), LRU first.
+        self.graphs: OrderedDict[Tuple[int, int], tuple] = OrderedDict()
+        self.seen: OrderedDict[Tuple[int, int], int] = OrderedDict()
+        self.failed_keys: set[Tuple[int, int]] = set()
+        self._pool: Any = None
+
+    def _record_hit(self, key: Tuple[int, int]) -> int:
+        count = self.seen.pop(key, 0) + 1
+        self.seen[key] = count
+        if len(self.seen) > self.capacity * 8:
+            self.seen.popitem(last=False)
+        return count
+
+    def run(self, patches: torch.Tensor, n_h: int, n_w: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        key = (n_h, n_w)
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            return self.encode(patches, n_h, n_w)
+        entry = self.graphs.get(key)
+        if entry is None:
+            if key in self.failed_keys or self._record_hit(key) < self.min_hits:
+                return self.encode(patches, n_h, n_w)
+            # No warm-up run: the earlier eager sightings warmed this grid.
+            entry = self._capture(key, patches)
+            if entry is None:
+                return self.encode(patches, n_h, n_w)
+        else:
+            self.graphs.move_to_end(key)
+        graph, static_patches, static_span, _ = entry
+        static_patches.copy_(patches)
+        graph.replay()
+        # Spans live on in the multimodal embedding cache; the next replay
+        # overwrites static_span.
+        return static_span.clone()
+
+    def _capture(self, key: Tuple[int, int], patches: torch.Tensor):
+        n_h, n_w = key
+        device = patches.device
+        static_patches = patches.clone()
+        # Built before capture so no host-to-device copy is recorded; the entry
+        # keeps them alive for as long as the graph reads them.
+        inputs = self.inputs(n_h, n_w, device)
+        if self._pool is None:
+            self._pool = torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle()
+        reserved_before = torch.cuda.memory_reserved(device)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        try:
+            # thread_local: other threads (e.g. the TP watchdog) keep running
+            # CUDA calls during capture.
+            with torch.cuda.graph(
+                graph, pool=self._pool, capture_error_mode="thread_local"
+            ):
+                static_span = self.encode(static_patches, n_h, n_w)
+        except Exception:
+            self.failed_keys.add(key)
+            logger.exception(
+                "DeepSeek-V4.1 ViT CUDA graph capture failed for grid %s; "
+                "using eager fallback",
+                key,
+            )
+            return None
+        entry = (graph, static_patches, static_span, inputs)
+        self.graphs[key] = entry
+        self.seen.pop(key, None)
+        if len(self.graphs) > self.capacity:
+            self.graphs.popitem(last=False)
+        logger.info(
+            "Captured DeepSeek-V4.1 ViT CUDA graph for grid %s (%d/%d), "
+            "reserved_delta_mib=%.1f",
+            key,
+            len(self.graphs),
+            self.capacity,
+            (torch.cuda.memory_reserved(device) - reserved_before) / 2**20,
+        )
+        return entry

@@ -0,0 +1,137 @@
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.models.deepseek_v41_vit import assemble_image_span
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.deepseek_v41_image_processing import image_token_types
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.deepseek_v41_vit_cuda_graph_runner import (
+    DeepseekV41ViTCudaGraphRunner,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("n_llm_h", "n_llm_w"), [(1, 1), (3, 5), (20, 19)])
+def test_assemble_image_span_matches_token_types(n_llm_h, n_llm_w):
+    d = 8
+    features = torch.randn(n_llm_h * n_llm_w, d)
+    start, newline, end = torch.randn(3, d).unbind(0)
+    types = image_token_types(n_llm_h, n_llm_w)
+    expected = torch.empty(len(types), d)
+    expected[types == 0] = start
+    expected[types == 1] = features
+    expected[types == 2] = newline
+    expected[types == 3] = end
+
+    span = assemble_image_span(features, n_llm_h, n_llm_w, start, newline, end)
+
+    assert torch.equal(span, expected)
+
+
+class _FakeGraph:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.replay_fn = None
+
+    def replay(self):
+        self.replay_fn()
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def fake_cuda_graph(monkeypatch):
+    """CPU stand-in: encode() registers what replay() recomputes in place."""
+    state = {"graph": None}
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def graph_context(graph, pool=None, capture_error_mode=None):
+        state["graph"] = graph
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            state["graph"] = None
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "CUDAGraph", _FakeGraph)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "graph", graph_context)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "graph_pool_handle", object)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", lambda: False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "memory_reserved", lambda _device: 0)
+
+    calls = {"eager": 0, "capture": 0}
+
+    def encode(patches, n_h, n_w):
+        out = patches * 2
+        graph = state["graph"]
+        if graph is None:
+            calls["eager"] += 1
+        else:
+            calls["capture"] += 1
+            graph.replay_fn = lambda: torch.mul(patches, 2, out=out)
+        return out
+
+    return encode, calls
+
+
+def test_graph_runner_captures_on_second_sighting(fake_cuda_graph):
+    encode, calls = fake_cuda_graph
+    runner = DeepseekV41ViTCudaGraphRunner(encode, lambda *_: None, min_hits=2)
+    patches = torch.randn(6, 4)
+
+    runner.run(patches, 2, 3)
+    assert calls == {"eager": 1, "capture": 0}
+    assert not runner.graphs
+
+    for _ in range(3):
+        assert torch.equal(runner.run(patches, 2, 3), patches * 2)
+    assert calls == {"eager": 1, "capture": 1}
+    assert list(runner.graphs) == [(2, 3)]
+
+
+def test_graph_runner_returned_spans_do_not_alias(fake_cuda_graph):
+    # Spans are kept in the multimodal embedding cache across later replays.
+    encode, _ = fake_cuda_graph
+    runner = DeepseekV41ViTCudaGraphRunner(encode, lambda *_: None, min_hits=1)
+    first_patches, second_patches = torch.randn(2, 6, 4).unbind(0)
+
+    first = runner.run(first_patches, 2, 3)
+    second = runner.run(second_patches, 2, 3)
+
+    assert torch.equal(first, first_patches * 2)
+    assert torch.equal(second, second_patches * 2)

+def test_graph_runner_failed_capture_stays_eager(fake_cuda_graph, monkeypatch):
+    encode, calls = fake_cuda_graph
+    runner = DeepseekV41ViTCudaGraphRunner(encode, lambda *_: None, min_hits=1)
+    attempts = []
+    spans = []
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def failing_graph(graph, pool=None, capture_error_mode=None):
+        attempts.append(True)
+        raise RuntimeError("operation not permitted when stream is capturing")
+        yield
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "graph", failing_graph)
+    patches = torch.randn(6, 4)
+
+    for _ in range(3):
+        spans.append(runner.run(patches, 2, 3))
+
+    assert attempts == [True]
+    assert calls["eager"] == 3
+    assert runner.failed_keys == {(2, 3)}
+    assert not runner.graphs
+    assert all(torch.equal(span, patches * 2) for span in spans)
+

+    runner = DeepseekV41ViTCudaGraphRunner(

+    )
+
+    for n_w in (1, 2, 1, 3):
+        runner.run(torch.randn(n_w, 4), 1, n_w)

+    assert list(runner.graphs) == [(1, 1), (1, 3)]
